display.purpose: Large dashboard KPI numerals and empty-state figures. Tabular. Rare.

body.purpose: Default UI text, table cells, form values — the workhorse (14px).

body-lg.purpose: Reading-heavy surfaces only (KB, AI answers); cap at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Form labels, table headers, metadata, timestamps.

code.purpose: IDs, serials, QR payloads, logs; JetBrains Mono, slashed zero.

shadows.name: overlay-sm
shadows.purpose: Floating overlays: dropdowns, popovers, comboboxes, context menus, tooltips.

shadows.name: overlay-md
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, modals, command palette. Never on inline cards.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Micro feedback: hover color, checkbox tick.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for state changes. No bounce, no elastic.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> crossfade or instant; no transforms

radius.name: full
radius.purpose: Status dots, avatars, toggle knobs only.

focusRing.purpose: Every focusable element, both modes. Never removed, never color-only.

narrative.overview: SccIT is the console an operations team sits in front of all day: a calm control room where quiet, dim surfaces let the instruments read clearly, information is packed onto the panels without feeling frantic, and exactly one indicator light means something the moment it turns on. Enterprise-first and productivity-over-decoration, taken literally: color is spent not sprinkled, depth is tone and hairlines rather than shadow, numbers are tabular, and the same control looks identical on every screen. It is vertical-agnostic by construction — it ships for schools first but re-skins for any organization by changing a single brand token, so identity is carried by structure and restraint, never by a motif that ties it to a classroom.
keyCharacteristics: Calm, dense, instrument-like: high information density with low visual noise.
Restrained color — a single brand signal (--primary) on <=10% of any surface.
Flat by tone: layered neutrals and hairline borders; shadow means 'floating overlay' only.
Dual-mode by construction: light ('day shift') and dark ('night shift') are equal citizens.
Vertical-agnostic: brand lives in one swappable token; nothing hard-codes 'school'.
WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor, verified — not a retrofit.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue covers <=10% of any screen — primary action, current selection, active nav, focus. Its rarity is what makes it read as a signal instead of a theme.

rules.name: The Reserved-Red Rule
rules.body: Red is only destructive, critical, or offline. It is never a brand color, decorative accent, or emphasis. A red that doesn't mean danger is a bug.

rules.name: The Swap-One-Token Rule
rules.body: Brand identity is --primary and its derived tints — nothing else. Re-skinning for a new organization is changing one hue. Status colors, neutrals, and type never carry vertical-specific identity.

rules.name: The Flat-Plane Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow means the element overlays the page (menu, dialog, toast, drag preview) — never an inline card or a lifted panel.

rules.name: The Tabular-Truth Rule
rules.body: Every numeric in a column, metric, ID, or timestamp uses tabular figures (and slashed zero for codes) so digits align and scan.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No tiny uppercase letter-spaced kicker above sections. Hierarchy is size and weight. Uppercase is permitted only on table column headers at <= +0.04em.

dos: Do spend Signal Blue like currency — primary action, current selection, active nav, focus — and let neutrals plus type carry the other ~90%.
Do build every deployment's brand from the single --primary token and its tints; keep status colors and neutrals vertical-neutral.
Do reserve red exclusively for destructive/critical/offline.
Do convey depth with the tonal stack (Canvas -> Panel -> Recess) and hairlines; use shadow only for floating overlays.
Do pair every status color with a text label and shape/icon so meaning survives color blindness and grayscale.
Do give every interactive element a visible 2px focus ring at 2px offset, and a full state set (hover/focus/active/disabled/loading).
Do use tabular figures for all columnar numbers, IDs, and timestamps.
Do keep both light and dark verified at WCAG 2.2 AA — re-check contrast whenever a token value changes.
donts: Don't use glassmorphism or neumorphism — no frosted-glass panels, no soft-extruded controls.
Don't over-animate the dashboard, add gaming-UI or crypto-dashboard flourishes, or orchestrated page-load sequences.
Don't use purple gradients — or gradient text of any kind. Emphasis is weight and size.
Don't pile on excessive shadows or make everything rounded; buttons and cards are 4-6px, not pills.
Don't ship visual clutter or 'Dribbble concepts' that prioritize aesthetics over usability.
Don't look like a generic AI-generated SaaS template: no cream/sand background, no tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow, no identical icon-card grids, no hero-metric template.
Don't use a colored border-left/border-right stripe as an accent — use a full border, a wash background, or a leading dot/icon.
Don't signal state with color alone, and never drop below AA — keep secondary text >=4.5:1.
Don't nest cards, or use a display/script font in labels, buttons, or data.
